back: The control plane builds the forwarding tables (routing protocols, STP). The data plane forwards traffic using those tables.

front: Which plane applies an ACL to a transit packet?
back: The data plane. Filtering, forwarding and VLAN tagging all act on traffic passing through the device.

front: Which plane do SSH, SNMP and syslog belong to?
back: The management plane: configuring and monitoring the device.

front: Where is the control plane in a traditional network and in a controller-based one?
back: Traditional: distributed, on every device. Controller-based: centralized in the controller. Devices forward traffic in both.
Policy, management and some or all control-plane decisions. Forwarding stays on the network devices.

front: The three SDN layers, bottom to top?

back: The controller's interface to the applications above it. It is usually a REST API over HTTPS.
The controller's interface to network devices. Examples: NETCONF, RESTCONF, OpenFlow, OpFlex, SNMP, SSH.
NETCONF: XML over SSH (TCP 830). RESTCONF: HTTPS with JSON or XML. Both use YANG data models.
The underlay is the physical IP network that carries the tunnels. The overlay is the virtual network built across it.
The underlay and overlay working together as one managed system, as in SD-Access.

front: Which UDP port and identifier does VXLAN use?
back: UDP destination port 4789. A 24-bit VNI identifies the virtual segment. VXLAN adds 50 bytes and does not encrypt.

front: SD-Access: which controller, control plane and data plane?
back: Catalyst Center (formerly DNA Center); LISP; VXLAN.

front: Which controller runs a Cisco ACI fabric, and what is the topology?
back: APIC, over a spine-leaf fabric: every leaf connects to every spine.

front: Name the five network management approaches.
back: Device-based, cloud-based, controller-based, automation-based and infrastructure as code. One deployment can be several at once.

front: How does automation change network management?
back: Changes are faster, identical on every device and recorded. A wrong input is also applied everywhere, so inputs are reviewed and results verified.
Network intent kept as version-controlled files that a tool applies, so changes are reviewed and repeatable.
A difference between the intended (desired) configuration and what the device is actually running.
Running the operation again gives the same end state and makes no further change.
